dedupe_keys.name: taipei long term projection of emergency ambulance demand to 2051 and the effect of temperature

description: This case study projects yearly emergency ambulance service demand in Taipei from 2015 to 2051 and how daily temperature will affect it as the population ages. The authors, researchers at National Cheng Kung University, National Taiwan Normal University and Hoa Sen University, used more than 140,000 patient records from the Taipei Fire Department for 2015, projected demand with changing age and sex structure, and modelled the relationship between daily average temperature and demand for 2036 and 2051; the work is published as an open-access journal article. Coverage is one city, with yearly and daily resolution. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence; the patient records are not public. Caveats: the base year is a single year, and future rates per age group are held at 2015 levels. The study found that ignoring population ageing underestimates 2051 demand for people over 65 by 42 to 90 percent and overestimates it for younger groups by 35 to 55 percent, and that the temperature-demand curve shifts upward and becomes more curved in 2051 once ageing is included. Simulation uses: demand scenarios for ambulance fleet and station planning under ageing and heat. Related records: the Ankara ambulance demand study (case_study-ankara-ambulance-demand-forecasting-capacity-planning) forecasts ambulance demand in another city.
